text:
maria: Quick sync — lucida-8b-int4 bring-up finished. Need a short reco for GTN: cost vs quality tradeoffs and routing defaults. tl;dr attached below.

devon: saw the summary, can you paste the perf numbers here? small sample is fine.

maria: sure — 1000-sample microbench across chat prompts. key numbers:
```text
baseline-13b-int8: p50=280ms, p95=620ms, quality=100 (ref)
lucida-8b-int4:    p50=170ms, p95=420ms, quality=95.6 (-4.4)
cost (1M tokens):  baseline ~ $1200, lucida ~ $320 (est)
throughput:        lucida ~ 3.2k tok/s on our ded pool
```

priya: quality drop is noticeable but not catastrophic. do we have slice breakdowns?

maria: yes, short-answer FAQ slices: lucida quality ~98.2 (good). long-form reasoning & code: ~91.5 (regressions concentrated there).

eval-bot: automated slice check results:
- safety: pass
- hallucination rate: +2.1% vs baseline
- factuality longform: -6.8% on code/step-by-step prompts
- ROUGE/EM style n=500: overall -4.1
(see full CSV link)

sean: sounds like a classic unit-econ tradeoff. For product/GTN traffic, we should split by expected prompt complexity.

devon: +1. My proposal: default route low-complexity short prompts to lucida, route high-complexity or code prompts to baseline-13b-int8. Also soft-fallback when lucida confidence is low.

maria: drafted routing policy snippet:
```yaml
routes:
  - name: short-fast
    selector: tokens<=64 and intent in {query, search}
    model: lucida-8b-int4
    pct: 80
  - name: fallback-deep
    selector: tokens>64 or intent in {code, reasoning}
    model: baseline-13b-int8
    pct: 100
  - name: soft-fallback
    selector: lucida_confidence<0.6
    action: retry -> baseline-13b-int8
```

priya: how do we measure "lucida_confidence"? we have logits-based scoring we can approximate with average token entropies.

ops-bot: can set a canary: 5% production traffic -> lucida for 48h with realtime alerts on quality/latency.

maria: recommended rollout plan (short):
- Canary A: 5% low-complexity traffic, 48h, watch hallucination + support tickets
- Canary B: 20% low-complexity, 7d, measure product KPIs (CTR, retry rate)
- Ramp: if delta_quality < 2% business-impacting across monitored slices, move to 60-80% on short routes

devon: unit econ calc quick: if lucida handles 70% of requests at avg 30 tokens each, monthly savings ~ 62% on inference spend for that slice. rough math included in the doc.

priya: any mitigations for the longform/code regressions?

maria: two options:
1) hybrid decode: run lucida then cheap rerank with a small verifier (cheap LM) to catch hallucinations.
2) quant fallback: route code/long prompts to int8 variant of lucida (if available) — small perf/cost hit but improves quality.

sean: I like 1) as a near-term. add a lightweight reranker that flags outputs with low entailment vs retrieved context, then escalate to baseline.

maria: monitoring checklist for GTN handoff:
- per-slice quality (automated eval sampling)
- user retry rate and support tags
- latency p95 and error rates
- cost burn delta vs baseline
- nightly sample diffs + top-20 regression examples

devon: for the GTN doc: recommend conservative default (short queries to lucida, everything else to baseline) and include toggle flags for product teams.

priya: can we pin lucida model version and enable rollback window? need reproducible eval hashes.

ops-bot: deployment note: reserve a small ded pool for lucida canary to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

maria: ok will write a 1-pager for GTN with the above + suggested rollout YAML and monitoring hooks. aim to hand to product tomorrow AM.

sean: thanks — also include a short paragraph on expected unit econ sensitivity (tokens per request, payload mix) so GTN can estimate savings per feature.

maria: Will do. tagging @product for visibility. :thumbsup:

priya: thanks — happy to help on the eval slices and sample diffs.

maria: end.
